transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-07-13 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Mercer, Priya Nambiar (Redwood)  Jordan Lee, Maya Patel, Samir Khan, Lina Torres (NexaHealth)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough): quick sync to go over the benchmark spreadsheet, p50/p95 numbers, compare to baseline provider, discuss tuning and next steps.

00:00 - Alex Mercer: okay everyone good morning, thanks for joining the weekly sync, quick roll call?
00:08 - Jordan Lee: hey Jordan here, Maya, Samir and Lina also on.
00:12 - Maya Patel: hi all, thanks.
00:15 - Priya Nambiar: Priya from Redwood, I'll run through the tuned config results then we can dig into p95.
00:22 - Alex Mercer: cool, so to orient, we tested three configs: hosted default, hosted with KV prefix cache, and a dedicated GPU pool with quantized model. We compared those to your baseline provider's numbers that you shared last week.
00:38 - Maya Patel: right, baseline is from CloudProviderX - their managed endpoint with our in-house sharding, approximate traffic mix we sent over.
00:46 - Priya Nambiar: first slide, p50 latency: baseline p50 was ~220ms for 512-token average workload, Redwood hosted tuned showed ~130ms, dedicated with quantization got down to ~95ms p50. These are median numbers across our 1k sample test.
01:05 - Samir Khan: hmm 95ms sounds great, is that end-to-end including network? our baseline numbers included their edge but not our VPC hop, so want to be apples-to-apples.
01:18 - Alex Mercer: good call, Samir. For our tests we included an egress hop to the same region; we used a test agent inside your VPC for the dedicated run, so it includes the internal hop. I can attach the raw logs.
01:29 - Jordan Lee: ok, what about p95? that's what bites us in production when spikes happen.
01:33 - Priya Nambiar: p95 is where it's mixed. Baseline p95 was ~540ms on your samples, Redwood hosted tuned p95 ~310ms, dedicated quantized p95 ~260ms. But when we ran 10k random traces, we saw higher tails  there are outliers when KV cache misses happen or on long context builds.
01:55 - Maya Patel: that aligns with what we saw, the baseline had fewer spikes apparently but overall higher medians. We care about both stable p50 and avoiding p99 spikes that break user sessions.
02:05 - Priya Nambiar: absolutely. A couple notes: our tuned config used dynamic batching with a 20ms latency cap, aggressive KV prefix caching for repeated prompts, and 4-bit quantization on the dedicated run which reduced token compute. That combo gives better median but the tail depends on your prompt distribution.
02:23 - Alex Mercer: also worth noting we saw throughput differences. Under sustained load (100 concurrent requests, 256 tokens avg) Redwood dedicated achieved ~950 reqs/sec with steady latency, baseline was around 700 reqs/sec before latency climbed.
02:39 - Samir Khan: 950 rps is promising. Did you test warm vs cold model warmup? our provider's warmup behavior is terrible, long TTLs.
02:47 - Priya Nambiar: yes, warm vs cold: cold start for dedicated is negligible after model resident, but hosted cold starts (when scaling to zero) add 1-2 seconds. We recommend pinned dedicated for production to avoid that.
02:59 - Jordan Lee: security and compliance  any differences if we go dedicated vs private? we'll need SOC2 and KMS integration.
03:06 - Alex Mercer: Redwood Dedicated gives reserved capacity and region-level isolation; Private (VPC/on-prem) gives control over networking and customer-managed KMS. We have SOC2 and ISO docs, we'll share the security packet after this call.
03:17 - Lina Torres: good, procurement will want that. Also curious about cost delta  quantization sounds great but what's the unit cost impact?
03:24 - Priya Nambiar: quantization reduces GPU memory and can double throughput in some cases, so unit token cost drops significantly on dedicated. We'll include rough cost estimates in the spreadsheet, but final numbers depend on your hit rate and cache effectiveness.
03:36 - Maya Patel: can you clarify the kv cache behavior? our prompts have a lot of prefix reuse between sessions.
03:42 - Priya Nambiar: KV prefix caching stores token keys for repeated prefixes so we avoid recomputing attention for common starters; on our tests we saw a 25-40% token compute reduction when prefix reuse was high. Misses still incur full compute which causes tail. We can tune TTLs and prefix matching heuristics for your workload.
04:00 - Jordan Lee: what about routing and fallback? if dedicated capacity is saturated, do we fall back to hosted?
04:06 - Alex Mercer: yes, smart routing policy can failover to hosted or a cheaper model variant automatically. For POC we had a fallback to hosted standard to keep latency bounded. That can be configured per route.
04:18 - Samir Khan: any artifacts you can share now? the spreadsheet, per-request logs, and the container config?
04:22 - Alex Mercer: yes sending after the call: benchmark spreadsheet link, raw logs (anonymized), and the config we used for tuning.
04:28 - Priya Nambiar: quick note  we observed one reproducible p99 spike tied to a 2048-token session that constructs the full KV cache; when we replicated that exact sequence the p99 hit ~1.6s on hosted but ~900ms on dedicated. We're investigating micro-optimizations in the runtime for large contexts.
04:48 - Maya Patel: that's the sort of case we need to eliminate. Many of our users do long-context sessions occasionally.
04:53 - Priya Nambiar: two options: pre-warm with larger batch windows for those flows or use dedicated quantized instances with larger memory to host the model resident. Both reduce tail. We'll run tests.
05:05 - Jordan Lee: timeline-wise our target is pilot to production in Q4. So we need clear actionables this month.
05:12 - Alex Mercer: agreed. For this week: we will run the expanded p95/p99 tests on 10k traces and share full logs; customer to return request distribution and typical prompt lengths; we'll schedule a deep-dive with SE for latency tuning.
05:25 - Lina Torres: procurement will also expect the SOC2 package and contract draft.
05:29 - Alex Mercer: noted, will send security packet and a preliminary pricing draft.
05:32 - Maya Patel: any open concerns about data residency or encryption?
05:35 - Priya Nambiar: for Dedicated you get region isolation, for Private we support customer-managed KMS/HSM  we can route keys to your KMS. We'll include KMS details in the packet.
05:46 - Jordan Lee: competitors  we ran similar tests against Anthropic and OpenAI?
05:49 - Priya Nambiar: we ran some informal baseline checks earlier; Anthropic had similar medians but higher tail for long context; OpenAI showed strong medians but cost is higher. These are high-level, not same workload.
06:00 - Samir Khan: ok that helps. Any blockers we should be aware of?
06:03 - Alex Mercer: main items are p95 tail tuning and confirmation of VPC networking constraints. Once we get your distribution we can recommend a committed Dedicated size.
06:12 - Maya Patel: cool. one more question  how reproducible are these numbers? we saw some variance across runs.
06:17 - Priya Nambiar: there's run-to-run variance due to network jitter and batch arrival patterns. That's why we want to run the larger 10k-sample tests and include multiple runs; we'll include mean/median/p95/p99 and standard deviation.
06:29 - Jordan Lee: excellent.
06:31 - Alex Mercer: wrapping up: recap of next steps  Alex to share artifacts (benchmark spreadsheet, security packet, pricing) by 2026-07-15; Priya to run larger latency runs and share by 2026-07-17; Maya to share request distribution by 2026-07-16; schedule deep-dive for week of 2026-07-20. Any final comments?
06:49 - Lina Torres: nope all good. thanks everyone.
06:52 - Maya Patel: thanks.
06:54 - Alex Mercer: thanks team, we'll follow up via email.

End of transcript.
